decisions.reason: The address autocomplete service builds on the firm's established data infrastructure, was publicly announced with its own page, and costs little to keep running, so dropping it would write off visible effort with little gain.

The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the firm's long-built industry databases into a new market, and that investment and public commitment would make withdrawal look like an admission of a failed expansion.
Peak load window determination is a regulated network-operator process central to the firm's announced platform direction, so management would persist and treat any weak uptake as temporary.
The end-customer tariff database sits close to the core market-data business that the firm has invested in for years, making it a strategic asset worth defending.
Custom web services fit the move toward SaaS and standardized data exchange, carry little stand-alone cost, and support the publicly stated platform strategy.
The postal code lookup service reuses existing geodata, has been presented publicly, and complements the address service, so the low upkeep and visible commitment favor keeping it.
